title: Selective-expert-checkpointing lands as default MoE save primitive by H2 2026
body: By the end of H2 2026 the consumer-tier MoE fine-tuning stack converges on selective-expert-checkpointing as the default save-time primitive across at least three of the major training frameworks, with Unsloth's v2026.5.26 release Tuesday establishing the operational template — checkpoint disk footprint for the MiniMax M2.7 235B MoE port collapsing from roughly 470GB to 188GB across the first ten saved revisions by freezing inactive expert columns on disk during write. The release is anchored by a paired Hugging Face Blog benchmark sheet from the Daniel Han Chen and Mike Han Chen author pair showing Qwen3.6-Max-Preview-235B training at roughly 1.74x throughput against the prior DeepSeek R3-Pro 38B recipe on a single 8x H200 SXM5 node, with peak combined VRAM falling 11.3 percent versus a vanilla Hugging Face Transformers v5 baseline. Two independent reproductions on CoreWeave and Crusoe Cloud 8x H200 SXM5 rentals landed inside 3 percent of the published numbers within the first trading day, and Simon Willison flagged the selective-expert-checkpoint primitive as the most operationally meaningful change shipped this quarter for downstream fine-tuners running against SSD budget caps on Lambda Labs or RunPod. The structural force is that once one mainstream trainer ships a save-time disk primitive that cuts MoE checkpoint footprint by ~60 percent without recipe rewrites and gets reproduced inside hours on multiple rental fleets, the rest of the consumer-tier training stack — Hugging Face TRL, Axolotl, Llama-Factory — has to either ship a compatible primitive or cede the 60B-to-235B-class MoE fine-tuning workload entirely, because the SSD-budget envelope is the binding constraint for paying tenants on Lambda Labs and RunPod once checkpoints cross the 200GB-per-revision line. Most likely landing is that by H2 2026 at least three of the major consumer-tier trainers (Unsloth plus two of TRL, Axolotl, or Llama-Factory) ship a save-time selective-expert-checkpoint primitive as a recipe-level default for MoE fine-tunes, with the contributed 60B-class-and-above recipe count crossing six across the cohort and at least one hyperscaler-managed fine-tuning service (AWS SageMaker, Google Vertex Custom Training, Azure ML) lighting up a managed tier that exposes it as a knob. Bear case is that one of the major trainers ships a competing block-sparse save format that fragments the standard before convergence, pushing the cross-trainer default into early 2027; absent that fragmentation, H2 2026 lands selective-expert-checkpointing as the de facto MoE save-time standard across the consumer-tier training cohort.

reasoning.because: Unsloth ships an expert-freeze checkpoint primitive cutting 235B MoE save disk ~60 percent.
reasoning.given: Two independent 8x H200 SXM5 reproductions landed inside 3 percent of the sheet within hours.
reasoning.so_that: Three or more consumer-tier trainers ship a save-time selective-expert primitive as MoE recipe default.
reasoning.landing: By H2 2026; Unsloth + two of TRL, Axolotl, Llama-Factory; one hyperscaler tier.
reasoning.plain_language: A new disk-saving trick for big MoE models shrinks save files about sixty percent, so other training tools will soon copy it.

summary: Unsloth's v2026.5.26 release ships a selective-expert-checkpoint primitive that cuts MiniMax M2.7 235B MoE checkpoint disk from ~470GB to ~188GB during save, with two independent 8x H200 SXM5 reproductions landing inside three percent. By H2 2026 three consumer-tier trainers default it.
